title: Lord! We Believe a Rest Remains
description: Lord! We Believe a Rest Remains in Tonic Solfa to ST. FLAVIAN, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Charles Wesley wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 479 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “A Rest Remaineth”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. FLAVIAN; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Lord! we be-lieve a rest re-mains To all thy peo-ple known; A rest where pure en-joy-ment reigns; For thou art served a-lone:

lines: Lord! we believe a rest remains
A rest where pure enjoyment reigns; —
A rest where all our souls desire
Where fear, and sin, and grief expire,
O that we now that rest might know,
Thou Holiest! now the power bestow,
And let us cease from sin.
Remove this hardness from our heart,
The rest of perfect faith impart,

licence: Public domain: Charles Wesley died in 1788.
credits: Words by Charles Wesley (1707–1788), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to ST. FLAVIAN by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
